pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +0.8%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $20.06 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 114 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-22.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-05) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: NumPy Tutorial: Your First Steps Into Data Science in Python
stories.excerpt: Follow this NumPy tutorial to learn how to create and manipulate arrays in Python and take your first steps into data science.
stories.lead: NumPy is a Python library that provides a simple yet powerful data structure: the n-dimensional array. stories.title: France braces for new protests, tightening security and boarding up shops
stories.excerpt: About 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, while Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu warned late on Friday that 'the threat' of violence 'remains high.'

stories.title: France prepares for day of protest a week after nationwide riots
stories.excerpt: Hundreds of thousands are expected to turn out, as more than 70,000 police officers are to be deployed over some may defy restrictions.
stories.lead:
France is on high alert ahead of a new day of nationwide protests on Saturday, a week after the country saw some of its worst unrest in decades.

Sweeping restrictions have been imposed on demonstrations across France but hundreds of thousands of protesters are still expected to gather in Paris and elsewhere for a second round of protests organised by students, trade unions and wider anti-government groups.

The interior ministry has said it will deploy 70,000 police officers, ramping up the security presence in French cities, after the government was accused by opposition parties of failing to foresee the scale of the unrest on 17 October.

stories.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
stories.excerpt: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.
stories.lead:
Drinking water has been scarce for over a decade in Taiz, but the problem has reached crisis levels in recent weeks as Iran-backed Houthi rebels besiege Yemen's third-largest city in their escalating conflict with government forces.

The needs of Taiz's more than 1 million residents are now barely being met, humanitarian groups say, as access to wells is limited, desalination plants run low on fuel and water delivery trucks are largely prevented from entering the city.

stories.title: White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
stories.excerpt: Ukraine and Russia confirm the truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents have had to eat garden weeds to survive.
stories.lead:
The White House statement said Melania Trump and one of her representatives had worked "directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire".

"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require," she is quoted as saying.

"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive co-ordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine."

stories.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
stories.excerpt: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.
stories.lead:
Looking out a window on Friday afternoon, Devin Neeley saw light, puffy clouds and a blue sky in San Juan County, N.M. The county's public information officer for emergency management called it "surreal."

Meanwhile, brown rainwaters were flooding homes in low-lying areas of the county and forcing sewage into the San Juan River.

"[The sky] belies really the danger that is coming down the river in historic levels," Neeley says. "We have not seen flooding like this in generations."

stories.title: At a Texas high school football game, fans offer a glimpse into evolving politics
stories.excerpt: We talk with voters at a Texas high school football game at the tailgate, in line at the concession booth and in the stands to hear about the issues that matter to Texans this cycle.
stories.lead:
Texas and football - a classic combination no matter who you root for.

DETROW: Root for or vote for. Texas has been a safe Republican state for three decades, but polling suggests next month's midterms could be tight. So Houston Public Media's Bianca Seward takes us to the bleachers at Deer Park High School's homecoming game, where fans in this Houston suburb offer a glimpse into the state's changing politics.

stories.title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
stories.excerpt: The chancellor will unveil AI spending aimed at shoring up the UK's defences in Wednesday's Budget.
stories.lead:
The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.

As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit £100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.

The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.

stories.title: How does the UK state pension compare with other countries?
stories.excerpt: Do British pensioners have it better or worse than those in other countries?
stories.lead:
Getting older is something few of us want to think about. Yet how we fund our later years, and how much we'll get, has been a hot topic.

The triple lock formula - state pensions increasing by the greatest of 2.5%, earnings growth, or inflation - means those benefits have risen far faster than the earnings of workers since its introduction in 2011.

But as housing costs have also been rising fast, pensioner poverty has actually increased slightly in the last decade.

stories.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
stories.excerpt: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.
stories.lead: AI researchers and international organizations have long advocated for strict regulation of AI when used in weapons that could become unpredictable or function with little human control, arguing that those tools could endanger the lives of soldiers and civilians and risk quickly escalating wars. But Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has repeatedly dismissed previous caution of AI tools and encouraged rapid autonomous innovation at the Pentagon.

stories.title: Title holder keeps perfect record
stories.excerpt: The eighth round of the Premier VRL League has been completed. In the final match, held at the Banjica pool in Belgrade, Radnicki defeated Partizan 12:8 […] The post Title holder keeps perfect record appeared first on Total Waterpolo .
stories.lead:
In the final match, held at the Banjica pool in Belgrade, Radnicki defeated Partizan 12:8 to maintain a perfect record. The team from Kragujevac secured the win during the third quarter.

Partizan entered the match against the favorites without fear, taking a 2:0 lead within the first three minutes. However, Radnicki then kept their defense “locked down” for nearly nine minutes, staging a turnaround with a 4:0 run. Partizan managed to level the score at 4:4, but the visiting team’s captain Andrija Prlainovic gave Radnicki a narrow 5:4 lead heading into the third period.

stories.title: Win Streak Snapped at Seven Games for Men's Water Polo
stories.excerpt: No. 18 Crimson fall in top-20 match-up with No. 13 Pacific.
stories.lead:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The No. 18 Harvard men's water polo team lost to No. 13 Pacific, 12-6, in its first game at the Julian Fraser Memorial Tournament hosted by Santa Clara. The Crimson saw its seven-game win streak snapped as it dropped to 10-11 on the season.

Juniors Lukas Peabody and Dean Strauser led Harvard with two goals and one assist apiece. Senior attacker Vilas Sogaard-Srikrishnan was pressed into action in the net again and provided 10 saves.

The Crimson are back in action on Saturday at 5:20 p.m. ET against No. 10 UC Davis.
